chunks: When you intend to depart for hajj, gather your family, perform two rak'ahs, glorify Allah abundantly, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and say: “O Allah, today I entrust to You my religion, my soul, my wealth, my family, my children, my neighbors, the people of my care, those present among us and those absent, and all that You have blessed me with. O Allah, place us in Your shelter, protection, refuge, and might. Mighty is Your protection and exalted is Your praise, and secure is the one who seeks refuge with You. There is no god but You. I rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die. Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a consort nor a child, and who has no partner in sovereignty, nor any protector out of humility, and magnify Him greatly. Allah is supremely great, and praise belongs to Allah abundantly, and glory be to Allah morning and evening.”

When you leave your house, say: “In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. There is no might nor power except by Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, the gloom of return, and an evil sight regarding family, wealth, and children. O Allah, in this journey I ask You for joy and for acting in that which pleases You of me. O Allah, remove from me its distance and hardship, accompany me in it, and be my successor among my family with goodness.” When you settle upon your mount and your conveyance is steady with you, say: “Praise be to Allah who guided us to Islam, taught us the Qur'an, and bestowed favor upon us through Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله. Glory be to Him who subjected this to us, though we were not capable of it, and indeed to our Lord we shall return. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, You are the carrier upon the back, the One sought for help in the matter; You are the companion in travel and the successor regarding family, wealth, and children. O Allah, You are my support and my helper.” When your mount proceeds with you, say on your way: “I have set out by Allah’s power and strength, without any power or strength from myself, but by Allah’s power and strength. I disavow before You, O my Lord, all power and strength. O Allah, I ask You for the blessing of this journey and the blessing of its people. O Allah, I ask You from Your vast bounty for lawful and wholesome provision that You drive toward me while I proceed in well-being by Your power and might. O Allah, I have traveled without any trust from myself in other than You and no hope in anyone besides You, so grant me in that Your gratitude and Your well-being, and grant me success for Your obedience and Your worship until You are pleased, and after pleasure.” Upon your journey, adhere to taqwa toward Allah, giving preference to His obedience, avoiding His disobedience, adopting noble character and deeds, good conduct, good companionship with those who accompany you, restraining anger, and increasing recitation of the Qur'an, the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and supplication.

When you reach one of the miqats appointed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, for he عليه السلام appointed al-'Aqiq for the people of Iraq—its beginning is al-Maslakh, its middle is Ghamrah, and its end is Dhat 'Irq, and its beginning is better; and he appointed Qarn al-Manazil for the people of al-Ta'if, Yalamlam for the people of Yemen, al-Mahya'ah which is al-Juhfah for the people of Syria, and Dhu al-Hulayfah which is Masjid al-Shajarah for the people of al-Madinah. Then perform ghusl after trimming your nails, taking from your moustache, plucking your armpits, and using depilatory. And when you perform ghusl, say: “In the Name of Allah and by Allah. O Allah, make it for me light, purification, protection, and safety from every fear, and healing from every illness and sickness. O Allah, purify me, purify my heart for me, expand my breast for me, and cause Your love, Your praise, and extolling You to flow upon my tongue. For there is no strength for me except through You, and I have known that the establishment of my religion is submission to Your command and following the sunnah of Your Prophet, Your blessings be upon him and his family.” Then put on your two garments of ihram and say: “Praise be to Allah who provided me with that by which I cover my nakedness, fulfill my duty, worship my Lord in it, and proceed in it to what He commanded me. Praise be to Allah whom I intended and He conveyed me, whom I desired and He helped me, who accepted me and did not cut me off, and whose direction I intended and He kept me safe. So He is my fortress, my cave, my protection, my support, my refuge, my shelter, my deliverance, my ذخيرة, and my provision in hardship and ease.”

Perform six rak'ahs for ihram, direct yourself in the first of them, and in each pair of rak'ahs recite in the first al-Hamd and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad, and in the second al-Hamd and Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun. Perform qunut in the second rak'ah of every two before ruku' and after recitation, and give taslim after every two rak'ahs. If you wish, you may pray two rak'ahs for ihram as described. The best times for ihram are at the sun’s decline, though it does not harm you whichever hour you enter ihram, at sunrise or sunset. If it is the time of an obligatory salat, then pray these rak'ahs before the obligation, then pray the obligatory salat, and enter ihram immediately after it so that it may be more excellent.

When you finish your prayer, praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, extol Him as He deserves, and send blessings and peace upon His Prophet Muhammad and his family, then say: “O Allah, I ask You to make me among those who answered You, believed in Your promise, and followed Your command. For I am Your servant and in Your grasp. I protect myself only from what You protect, and I take only what You give. O Allah, I intend what You have commanded of tamattu' with 'umrah to hajj according to Your Book and the sunnah of Your Prophet, Your blessings be upon him and his family. If some impediment occurs to me and restrains me, then release me where You restrain me, by Your decree which You have decreed upon me. O Allah, and if it is not a hajj, then an 'umrah. I enter ihram for You with my hair, my skin, my flesh, my blood, my bones, my marrow, and my sinews, abstaining from women and perfume, seeking by that Your noble Face and the final abode.” It suffices you to say this once when you enter ihram.

key_terms.إِحْرَامِكَ: the sacred state entered for hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.التَّمَتُّعِ: the hajj form combining 'umrah before hajj
key_terms.الطِّيبِ: perfume, from which the muhrim abstains
key_terms.الْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage to the Sacred House and its rites
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an, to be recited frequently during the journey
key_terms.الْمَوَاقِيتِ: the designated stations where ihram is to be assumed
key_terms.تَقْوَى: God-conscious piety expressed through obedience and restraint

ai.seo_question: What supplications and ritual steps should be performed before departing for hajj and when entering ihram?
ai.summary: This text outlines the recommended acts, supplications, and ritual procedures for setting out to hajj and entering ihram. It combines legal guidance on miqats, ghusl, salat, and ihram with supplications emphasizing tawhid, reliance upon Allah, and upright conduct during travel.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
If you intend to embark on Hajj, gather your family, perform two units of prayer, glorify Allah (swt) abundantly, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family, and say:
"O Allah (swt), I entrust to You today my religion, myself, my wealth, my family, my children, my neighbors, those who are present among us, those who are absent, and all the blessings You have bestowed upon me. O Allah (swt), place us under Your protection, safeguarding, refuge, and might. Mighty is Your protection, exalted is Your praise, and inviolable is Your refuge. There is no deity other than You. I rely on the Living, who does not die. All praise is due to Allah (swt), who has not taken a consort or a child, who has no partner in His dominion, and who has no helper out of weakness. And magnify Him with due magnification. Allah (swt) is the Greatest, abundantly great. All praise is due to Allah (swt) in abundance. Glory be to Allah (swt) in the morning and evening."

When you leave your home, say:
"In the name of Allah (swt), the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. There is no power or strength except with Allah (swt), the Most High, the Most Great. O Allah (swt), I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travel, the sorrow of return, and unpleasant sights concerning my family, wealth, and children. O Allah (swt), I ask You in this journey for joy and deeds that earn Your pleasure. O Allah (swt), spare me its distance and its difficulties. Be my companion in it and leave goodness in my family in my absence."
When you mount your ride and it settles under you, say:
"All praise is due to Allah (swt), who guided us to Islam, taught us the Quran, and favored us with Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him and his family). Glory be to the One who subjected this to us, for we could not have controlled it ourselves, and indeed, to our Lord (azj), we shall return. All praise is due to Allah (swt), the Lord (azj) of all the worlds. O Allah (swt), You are the one who carries us on this mount, the One from whom we seek help in our affairs. You are the companion in travel and the guardian of family, wealth, and children. O Allah (swt), You are my support and my helper."
When your mount moves you along your journey, say on your way:
"I have set out by the will and power of Allah (swt), not by any will or power of my own, but through the will and power of Allah (swt). I renounce my own will and power before You, O Lord (azj). O Allah (swt), I ask You for blessings in this journey and blessings for its people. O Allah (swt), I ask You, by Your expansive bounty, for lawful, wholesome, and pure provision, which You will send to me while I proceed in ease and well-being, by Your power and ability. O Allah (swt), I have undertaken this journey not relying on myself but entirely trusting in You, and not placing hope in anyone other than You. So, grant me in this journey gratitude towards You, Your protection, and success in Your obedience and worship until You are pleased with me and after Your pleasure is achieved."
On your journey, observe piety towards Allah (swt), prefer His obedience, avoid disobedience, and practice noble character and actions. Be kind and companionable to those who travel with you, control your anger, recite the Quran frequently, remember Allah (swt), and make supplications.

When you reach one of the Miqats (stations for assuming Ihram) designated by the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family)—he designated:
•	For the people of Iraq, Al-‘Aqiq, with its beginning at Al-Maslakh, its middle at Ghamrah, and its end at Dhat ‘Irq (the beginning is the best).
•	For the people of Ta’if, Qarn al-Manazil.
•	For the people of Yemen, Yalamlam.
•	For the people of Syria, Al-Juhfah, also known as Al-Mihyah.
•	For the people of Medina, Dhu al-Hulayfah, which is the Mosque of the Tree.
Perform ghusl (ritual bath) after trimming your nails, shortening your mustache, plucking your armpits, and cleansing yourself.
When performing ghusl, say:
"In the name of Allah (swt), and by Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), make this (ghusl) a light for me, a purification, a protection, and a security from every fear, and a cure from every illness and sickness. O Allah (swt), purify me, purify my heart for me, expand my chest, and make my tongue flow with Your love, praise, and glorification. For I have no power except through You, and I know that the foundation of my religion lies in submission to Your command and following the Sunnah of Your Prophet, peace be upon him and his family."
Then wear the two garments of Ihram and say:
"All praise is due to Allah (swt), who provided me with what covers my private parts, enables me to fulfill my obligations, worship my Lord (azj), and comply with His commands. All praise is due to Allah (swt), whom I sought, and He allowed me to reach Him; whom I desired, and He aided me; who accepted me and did not abandon me; and whose direction I sought, and He granted me safety. He is my fortress, my refuge, my protection, my support, my shelter, my sanctuary, my provision, my reserve in hardship and ease."

Perform six units of prayer (rak’ahs) for Ihram, directing yourself to Allah (swt) in the first of them. In each pair of units, recite in the first unit Surah Al-Hamd (Al-Fatihah) and Surah Al-Ikhlas (Say: He is Allah (swt), the One), and in the second unit Surah Al-Hamd and Surah Al-Kafirun (Say: O disbelievers). Perform the qunut in the second unit of each pair before bowing (ruku’) and after reciting the Surahs. Conclude with salutations (taslim) after every two units. If you wish, you may perform just two units of prayer for Ihram as described.
The best time for entering Ihram is when the sun declines from its zenith, but it does not matter at what hour you assume Ihram, whether at sunrise or sunset. If it coincides with the time for an obligatory prayer, perform the six units before the obligatory prayer, then perform the obligatory prayer, and assume Ihram immediately after it for added merit.

When you have completed your prayer, praise Allah (swt), glorify Him as He deserves, and send blessings upon His Prophet Muhammad and his family. Then say:
"O Allah (swt), I ask You to make me among those who respond to You, believe in Your promise, and follow Your command. I am Your servant, in Your grasp. I can only be protected by what You protect me from, and I can only receive what You grant me. O Allah (swt), I intend to fulfill what You have commanded, by performing Tamattu’ with Umrah leading to Hajj, according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family. If an obstacle arises that prevents me, then release me where You prevent me, according to what You have decreed for me. O Allah (swt), if this is not a Hajj, then let it be an Umrah. I dedicate my hair, my skin, my flesh, my blood, my bones, my marrow, and my nerves to You, away from women and perfume, seeking thereby Your noble countenance and the Hereafter."
It suffices to say this once when assuming Ihram.
